overview: After 1.e4 e5 2.f4 exf4 White plays 3.Kf2, the Tumbleweed or Drunken King, avoiding Qh4+ by walking the king. Black keeps the pawn with ...d5 or ...Nf6 and White pursues Nf3, Bc4 and quick development. Mostly seen in blitz and surprise play.

white_ideas.idea: Develop with Nf3 and Bc4 hitting f7
Regain the f4 pawn and use the open f-file

black_ideas.idea: Keep the extra pawn with ...d5 or ...g5
Develop and use the exposed king on f2

typical_structures.structure: Open centre, White king on f2, Black pawn on f4

character.notes: Open play with exposed king; forcing tactics early.

gambit.notes: The f4 pawn is given and Black can keep it.

soundness.notes: The king walk is regarded as too risky.

character.reason: An exposed king and open lines make this fully tactical.

gambit.reason: White gave up f4 in the King's Gambit and Black can keep it.

soundness.reason: The king walk is considered too risky.

structure.reason: The e-pawn is gone and the f-file is open.

approach.reason: Strong players rarely play the Tumbleweed.

plans.reason: White's compensation is quick development and pressure on f7.
